newsitem.title: GERMANY: Police detain suspect in German arson attack.
newsitem.headline: Police detain suspect in German arson attack.

text.p: Police on Sunday detained a 33-year-old suspect after a fire on church property in the city of Luebeck, the latest in a string of extremist arson attacks in northern Germany.
A police spokesman said the man's car had been sighted close to the scene of the blaze -- a kindergarten in a Christian community centre which also includes a church.
Investigators found Nazi swastikas sprayed on the walls of the building and a slogan threatening local priest Guenter Harig, a well-known campaigner for the rights of asylum-seekers.
The fire caused some damage but no one was injured and firefighters extinguished the blaze within 30 minutes.
"Harig, we'll get you" the slogan read. The churchman's name was also found daubed at the scene of an attack in Luebeck last month, which destroyed a Roman Catholic church.
A 19-year-old man has been detained on suspicion of that attack.
On June 4, a Protestant church in Hamburg was set on fire after being daubed with right-wing and Satanic symbols but the building was only slightly damaged.

Police detained a 44-year-old man in connection with an arson attack on a church in the town of Husum two weeks ago. Investigators found a note on the church door which they said was both anti-Semitic and anti-Christian.

Earlier this week, vandals spray-painted swastikas on the Luebeck office of Germany's best known author, Guenter Grass, and on another local church. The left-leaning novelist had publicly backed Harig's social campaigning.
The suspect's car was spotted near the community centre soon after the attack, police said.

When officers came to question him at his home, he climbed up onto the roof and threatened to jump. The man, a scaffolder, later agreed to come down and was placed in custody. Police said it was so far unclear if the attacker had acted alone.
